links.outcome: OPS-code extraction accuracy, hallucinations and total mistakes
links.effect: Specified meningioma coding rules (GPT-5r): accuracy 79% vs 44% for GPT-5s; hallucinations 8 vs 105; mistakes 21 vs 132 (p < 0.001)
links.quote: We show, that specific context enhancement significantly improves GPT-5s ability to perform OPS-code extraction from operational reports, while significantly lowering mistake- and hallucination rates.

links.comparator_used: GPT-5 with no additional context (GPT-5s), and GPT-5 with the OPS catalogue only (GPT-5o)
links.outcome: OPS-code extraction accuracy, hallucinations and mistakes
links.effect: Code-triggering sample phrases from 50 additional reports (GPT-5e): accuracy 70% vs 44% for GPT-5s; hallucinations 2 vs 105; mistakes 35 vs 132 (p < 0.001)
links.tradeoff: GPT-5e produced more mistakes than the rules-based GPT-5r (35 vs 21; GPT-5r had fewer, p = 0.034). Building the phrases required 50 additional operative reports.
links.quote: Non context enhanced GPT-5s showed the lowest rate of correct coding (44%) and highest number of hallucinations (105) and total mistakes (132).

design_hint: context enhancement (catalogue, rules, example phrases) via prompt grounding
